arxiv-2107-04100.title: SoS certification for symmetric quadratic functions and its connection to constrained Boolean hypercube optimization Thanks: Adam Kurpisz was supported by SNSF project PZ00P2 _ \_ 174117, Aaron Potechin was supported in part by NSF grant CCF2008920.
arxiv-2107-04100.creator: Adam, Kurpisz, Aaron, Potechin, Elias Samuel, Wirth
arxiv-2107-04100.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Adam, Kurpisz, Aaron, Potechin, Elias Samuel, Wirth. We study the rank of the Sum of Squares (SoS) hierarchy over the Boolean hypercube for Symmetric Quadratic Functions (SQFs) in n n variables with roots placed in points k − 1 k-1 and k k . Functions of this type have played a central role in deepening the understanding of the performance of the SoS method for various unconstrained Boolean hypercube optimization problems, including the Max Cut problem.

arxiv-2201-01946.title: Nondivergent deflection of light around a photon sphere of a compact object
arxiv-2201-01946.creator: Ryuya Kudo, Hideki Asada
arxiv-2201-01946.description: Abstract We demonstrate that the location of a stable photon sphere (PS) in a compact object is not always an edge such as the inner boundary of a black hole shadow, whereas the location of an unstable PS is known to be the shadow edge notably in the Schwarzschild black hole.

arxiv-2301-01451.title: Reduced dynamics with Poincaré symmetry in an open quantum system
arxiv-2301-01451.creator: Akira Matsumura
arxiv-2301-01451.description: Abstract We consider how the reduced dynamics of an open quantum system coupled to an environment admit the Poincaré symmetry. The reduced dynamics are described by a dynamical map, which is a quantum channel (a completely positive and trace-preserving linear map) given by tracing out the environment from the total unitary evolution without initial correlations.

Solids 2000; 48:175–209) composite materials (CMs) of the random and periodic structures are considered. In the framework of the second background of micromechanics (also called computational analytical micromechanics, CAM), one proved that local micromechanics (LM) and peridynamic micromechanics (PM) are formally similar to each other for CM of both random and periodic structures. It allows for the straightforward generalization of LM methods to their PM counterparts.

arxiv-2402-14224.title: Framing in the Presence of Supporting Data: A Case Study in U.S. Economic News
arxiv-2402-14224.creator: Alexandria Leto Elliot Pickens Coen D. Needell, David Rothschild Maria Leonor Pacheco
arxiv-2402-14224.description: Abstract The mainstream media has much leeway in what it chooses to cover and how it covers it. These choices have real-world consequences on what people know and their subsequent behaviors. However, the lack of objective measures to evaluate editorial choices makes research in this area particularly difficult.

arxiv-2411-15991.title: Nitrogen-Vacancy Color Centers in Nanodiamonds as Reference Single-Photon Emitters
arxiv-2411-15991.creator: Nikesh Patel, 1 Benyam Dejen, 2 Stephen Church, 1,* Philip Dolan 2,3 and Patrick Parkinson 1
arxiv-2411-15991.description: Abstract Quantitative and reproducible optical characterization of single quantum emitters is crucial for quantum photonic materials research, yet accounting for measurement conditions remains challenging due to a lack of an established reference standard. We propose nanodiamonds containing single nitrogen vacancy (NV - ) color centers as reliable, stable and robust reference sources of single-photon emission.

arxiv-2412-06754.title: Probability and Angelic Nondeterminism with Multiset Semantics
arxiv-2412-06754.creator: Shawn Ong, Stephanie Ma, Dexter Kozen
arxiv-2412-06754.description: Abstract . We introduce a version of probabilistic Kleene algebra with angelic nondeterminism and a corresponding class of automata. Our approach implements semantics via distributions over multisets in order to overcome theoretical barriers arising from the lack of a distributive law between the powerset and Giry monads.

arxiv-2508-08293.title: Topos Theory for Generative AI and LLMs Thanks: Draft under submission.
arxiv-2508-08293.creator: Sridhar Mahadevan
arxiv-2508-08293.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sridhar Mahadevan. We propose the design of novel generative AI architectures (GAIA) using topos theory , a type of category that is “set-like": a topos has all (co)limits, is Cartesian closed, and has a subobject classifier. Previous theoretical results on the Transformer model have shown that it is a universal sequence-to-sequence function approximator, and dense in the space of all continuous functions on ℝ d × n \mathbb{R}^{d\times n} with compact support.

arxiv-2508-17312.title: Study Entropy of L-algebras
arxiv-2508-17312.creator: Mohamad Ebrahimi, Arsham Borumand Saeid
arxiv-2508-17312.description: Abstract In this paper, the concept of L-algebra is revisited and after that, the article is prepared to deal with the notion of the entropy of an L-algebra. If a set has an L-algebraic structure, it is possible to calculate the degree of uncertainty for an event called partition.

arxiv-2509-15724.title: RMT-KD : Random Matrix Theoretic Causal Knowledge Distillation
arxiv-2509-15724.creator: Davide Ettori 1 , Nastaran Darabi 1 , Sureshkumar Senthilkumar 1 , and Amit Ranjan Trivedi 1
arxiv-2509-15724.description: Abstract Large deep learning models such as BERT and ResNet achieve state-of-the-art performance but are costly to deploy at the edge due to their size and compute demands. We present RMT-KD , a compression method that leverages Random Matrix Theory (RMT) for knowledge distillation to iteratively reduce network size.

arxiv-2602-16350.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing via spectral noise reduction
arxiv-2602-16350.creator: Romain Dalidet 1 , Sébastien Tanzilli 1 , Audrey Dot 2 , Inès Ghorbel 2 , Loïc Morvan 2 , Laurent Labonté 1, Anthony Martin 1
arxiv-2602-16350.description: Abstract We report a direct demonstration of quantum-enhanced sensing in the Fourier domain by comparing single- and two-photon interference in a fiber-based interferometer under strictly identical noise conditions. The simultaneous acquisition of both signals provides a common-mode reference that enables a fair and unambiguous benchmark of quantum advantage.

pmc-12473256.title: An Analytical Model of Motion Artifacts in a Measured Arterial Pulse Signal—Part I: Accelerometers and PPG Sensors
pmc-12473256.creator: Md Mahfuzur Rahman, Subodh Toraskar, Mamun Hasan, Zhili Hao, Giovanni Saggio
pmc-12473256.description: This paper, the first of two parts, presents an analytical model of motion artifacts (MAs) in measured pulse signals by accelerometers and photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors. As the transmission path from the true pulse signal in an artery to the sensor output (measured pulse signal), the tissue–contact–sensor (TCS) stack is modeled as a 1DOF (degree-of-freedom) system.

pmc-12657227.title: Beyond swimming: emerging parameters for predicting the fertility of mouse spermatozoa
pmc-12657227.creator: Nataliia Shapovalova, Thorsten Buch, Heinrich Bollwein, Johannes vom Berg, Eleni Malama
pmc-12657227.description: Cryopreservation of spermatozoa can be used as a cost-effective way of preserving the ever-increasing number of genetically modified mouse lines. Nevertheless, discontinuing the breeding of a line or strain is only warranted after the quality control of cryopreserved sperm; the ability of sperm to survive the freezing–thawing process and produce well-developed embryos needs to be confirmed.

pmc-12663444.title: Silicate chemical weathering disrupts the global patterns of phosphorus limitation
pmc-12663444.creator: Chaojun Li, Xi Lu, Jingan Chen, Qiu Tan, Guangjie Luo, Luhua Wu, Fei Chen, Chen Ran, Sirui Zhang, Lian Xiong, Chaochao Du, Fengjiao Song, Biqin Xiao, Zilin Li, Yingying Xue, Mingkang Long, Xiaoyong Bai
pmc-12663444.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Global change is accelerating the chemical weathering of silicate rocks and the associated phosphorus release. However, the effects of phosphorus release on the global patterns of plant phosphorus limitation remain unclear. Here, we show that approximately 47% of the exposed areas in global silicate rocks are subject to phosphorus limitation of vegetation growth, as estimated using the ratio of leaf nitrogen to phosphorus resorption efficiency.

pmc-12732522.title: Raman and Infrared Spectroscopy of Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries
pmc-12732522.creator: Christian M Julien, Alain Mauger, Giovanni Battista Appetecchi
pmc-12732522.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Vibrational spectroscopy is one of the most powerful techniques available for the characterization of materials for Li-ion batteries (LIBs) and one of the most useful tools when X-ray diffraction is ineffective for amorphous substances. Raman spectroscopy is essentially a probe to examine the surface of compounds that strongly absorb visible light, which is the case for all electrode materials, while infrared spectroscopy is a tool that examines the entire volume of particles.

pmc-13076126.title: Family dynamics in Filipino transnational families: the role of non-migrant mothers
pmc-13076126.creator: Peachy Domingo
pmc-13076126.description: Since the 1970s, large-scale Filipino migration has led to the long-term absence and global dispersal of family members, giving rise to Filipino transnational families. This separation affects family stability and interpersonal relationships, yet many families maintain strong bonds across borders. However, the crucial role of non-migrant mothers in sustaining family cohesion often remains overlooked.

pmc-13695475.title: Epilepsy educational curriculum for nurses: A report from the Nursing Section of the International League Against Epilepsy
pmc-13695475.creator: Patricia O. Shafer, Sandra Dewar, Ariane Bernier, Ludivine Rohrer, Nancy Santilli, Carmela Redhead, Tammy Gravel, Gagandeep Singh, Jane R. von Gaudecker
pmc-13695475.description: A comprehensive, competency‐based epilepsy curriculum is needed to strengthen nurses' capacity to care for people with epilepsy worldwide. Such a curriculum should be adaptable across nursing roles, practice settings, and geographic regions. This report describes the development of a nursing curriculum for the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE).

uslaw-usc-t18-s1655.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1655 — Assault on commander as piracy
uslaw-usc-t18-s1655.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s1655.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 81 (Piracy And Privateering). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever, being a seaman, lays violent hands upon his commander, to hinder and prevent his fighting in defense of his vessel or the goods intrusted to him, is a pirate, and shall be imprisoned for life.
